theory: Threshold model of firms' data portfolios (working paper under review; author and title withheld for blind review)
adapted_from: Gimeno, Folta, Cooper, and Woo (1997), Administrative Science Quarterly 42(4)

variables.x1: generalizable share of the data portfolio, range [0, 1]
variables.x3: total size of the data portfolio, range [0, 10]
variables.x2: identity: (1 - x1) * x3, stock of product-market-specific data

threshold: T_C = PM_A(x1 x3) + DV_A(x1 x3, tau) - DV_C(x2, tau) - RC(x4)
exit_rule: exit if PM_C < T_C - W, where W is the value of waiting (W = 0 without uncertainty)

propositions.P1: d(T_C - PM_C) / dx1 > 0, holding x3 fixed
propositions.P2: sign of d(T_C - PM_C) / dx3 depends on whether the threshold effect of generalizable data exceeds the gain in focal-market value
propositions.footnote_3: P1 is robust to the value of waiting unless W varies enough with x1 to reverse it

functional_forms.PM_C: b + aC * x3^thC * (1 - x1 + g * x1)
